items.statement: Receivables increased to INR9.9 crores (58 days), up 26 days from March 2024
items.quote: On working capital front, our receivables were at INR9.9 crores. Translating into 58 days, this is an increase of 26 days vis-a-vis March 24.

items.statement: Auditors guided management to restate EV leasing accounting from operating lease to finance lease, impacting historical financials.
items.quote: As Anmol mentioned before, management, as guided by the auditors, have restated accounting treatment of EV leasing business. We will be treating some of the assets under this segment as finance lease versus the operating lease that was treated earlier.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of Rs. 154 crores generated in H1 FY25 due to working capital reduction in solar business.
items.quote: which resulted in generation of cash flow from operations to the tune of Rs. 154 crores.

items.statement: Total unencumbered cash balance is Rs. 258 crores as of 30th September 2024.
items.quote: The total unencumbered cash balance is Rs. 258 Crore.

items.statement: Equity increased by Rs. 200 crores driven by allocation of warrants on a preferential basis.
items.quote: This period also saw an increase in equity, basically driven by allocation of warrants on a preferential basis.

items.statement: Shareholder approval obtained for a QIP of Rs. 750 crores; company is preparing for the issue.
items.quote: We have shareholder approval to do a QIP for Rs. 750 crores and we are prepping up the company for that and in due course we will do the Rs. 750 crore QIP.

items.statement: Company uses packing credit at ~5% interest secured by orders in hand
items.quote: The Company has taking Packing Credit limit on lower interest around 5% as business decision. The said loan will be fully secured by orders in hands and will be paid timely.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR 50 crore equity by March for branch expansion and loan book growth
items.quote: Therefore, we will raise INR 50 crores in equity.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to execution of a large PSU bank order and milestone-linked payments; collection expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: One, definitely we have executed a new order of one of the large public sector banks, where we have executed and delivered the project and now the realisation will happen in the quarter three.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances (FDs and mutual funds) at Rs 63 crore in Q2 FY25 vs Rs 60 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: our bank balances in terms of bank fixed deposits and investment in mutual funds as part of treasury Operations. We stand at Rs. 63 crore as against Rs. 60 crore in Q1.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased substantially in H1 FY25 purely for working capital due to business growth and longer credit periods.
items.quote: Borrowing is only working capital. There is no CAPEX. There is nothing of any other usage, but it is purely being used for working capital.

items.statement: Management is trying to reduce credit periods and receivables to minimum days despite business growth.
items.quote: We are trying to reduce the credit periods and the receivables. We are trying to minimize to minimum days, but still, since the business is growing quite a lot.

items.statement: Acquisition of LCL company will involve majority stake and management control with growth funding provided.
items.quote: We are looking at a company which has closer to around maybe 100 plus crores of business topline where we can acquire. We don't want to run it ourselves. We want the company, maybe have management control, we have a majority stake in that and providing them with growth fund.

items.statement: Capital raised this quarter already deployed with minimal negative carry expected
items.quote: this quarter’s capital has already been deployed. When the results come ou t, you’ll see that we don’t expect much negative carry, if any —maybe ₹3-4-5 crore, but nothing major

items.statement: Promoter stake sale agreement with LT1 Inc. expired and no renewal talks are ongoing.
items.quote: So that is what I discussed that that share purchase agreement got expired which we as a promoter and LT1 signed.

items.statement: LT1 Inc. holds 3.8% stake in DEV IT and could not acquire promoter stake due to internal arrangements.
items.quote: So that's what LT1 we already received a couple of orders but the stake remained 3.8%, as of now they could not able to acquire a promoter stake s due to their internal arrangement with the financial institution.

items.statement: Working capital requirement expected to be around Rs 7,200 crores due to acquisitions and North America expansion.
items.quote: So, we are expecting around 7,200 crores of working capital because of acquiring couple of companies as well as having our own physical presence in North American market.

items.statement: Management announced a preferential issue of up to 300,000 equity shares priced per SEBI guidelines to fund R&D facilities.
items.quote: To support these developments, we are initiating a preferential issue up to 3,00,000 equity shares with pricing in line with service guideline.

items.statement: Demerger final order expected on 29th November; effective date may be 1st February after ROC formalities
items.quote: Demerger, the final order is expected to come on 29 th of November. So once the order comes, then there will be some formalities with ROC. So may be from 1 st February, we will see the effective date for demerger.

items.statement: Receivables jump is seasonal due to peak quarter volumes and short-term processing cycle of 1-2 days
items.quote: See, whenever there is a peak season, there is always a time difference before -- as I said, we handle huge amount of remittances. We handle huge amount of corporate business. So these are all short -term credits which come in. And the volume also has gone up considerably. Every September, you will see this happening because of seasonality.

name: Shri Keshav Cements And Infra Ltd

items.statement: Solar EBITDA of Rs 14 crore in H1 FY25 offset negative cement EBITDA, resulting in consolidated EBITDA of Rs 11.11 crore
items.quote: The solar EBITDA is around 14 crores, and the cement EBITDA is negative, which is why we have seen 11.11 crores.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of 30,77,800 equity shares at Rs 108 per share raising Rs 33.24 crore
items.quote: The recent preferential allotment of 3077800 equity shares at ₹108 per share totaling ₹33.24 Crore, will further strengthen our financial position to support these growth plans.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of 30 September 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free as on 30 September 2024.

items.statement: Company received first 25% tranche of QIP proceeds (~INR37 crore) and is using it for working capital and capex
items.quote: We have only taken, first 25% of money has come in, which is amounting to about INR37 crores. And most of it is getting utilized either in working capital or capex.

items.statement: Equity raise of INR176 crores completed, comprising INR63 crores equity and INR113 crores warrants, with INR91 crores received in Q2 and INR85 crores receivable before March 2026.
items.quote: We also reached equity of INR176 crores which is more than double our net worth in Q1, out of which INR63 crores equity and 113 was warrants and INR91 crores is already received in second quarter and balance INR85 crores is receivable before March 26.

items.statement: ESOP expenditure of INR0.1 million recognized in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Net loss for the quarter was INR11.2 million, partially due to INR0.1 million of ESOP expenditure and exceptional items.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 43.9 crore preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants in Q4 FY24; Rs 28.9 crore received by end-March for equity shares and 25% of warrants.
items.quote: In the 4th Quarter of FY24, the board of directors approved the infusion of Rs. 43.9 crores of equity by the way of preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants.

items.statement: Debtor days increased to 42 days from 39 days average last year.
items.quote: Our debtor days stood at 42 days, up from the average of 39 days in the last year.

items.statement: Inventory days rose to 156 days of consumption from 149 days due to finished goods build-up.
items.quote: Inventory days has also increased to 156 days of consumption as compared to 149 days of consumption, largely on account of build-up of finished goods inventory.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle increased to 122 days in H1 FY25 from 79 days in FY24.
items.quote: As a result, the cash conversion cycle has been increased to 122 days in H1 FY25 from 79 days in FY24.

items.statement: Recent fundraise was for subsidiary project cost overruns and working capital needs; HPMC line funding was never a constraint
items.quote: The recent fundraise was as informed to the stock exchange was mainly for two purposes. One was to contribute to the subsidiary company because of the increase in the project outlay there and delay in implementation. There was some cost implications, which the company has taken care of. Second is, of course, to beef up our working capital requirement and that would help us to meet the higher top l

items.statement: Receivable days increased to ~140 days due to clients diverting funds for plant upgrades and MSME payment preferences; gross sales basis ~112 days
items.quote: Actually, this is the area of concern for us as well because actually what is happening in pharma industry, there is a government deadline for 31st December to upgrade their plants. So, many of our clients are holding payments, diverting all their funds towards facility improvement.

items.statement: Additional credit loss provision of ~35 lakhs made in H1 FY25; company says fully covered and no major P&L impact expected
items.quote: on the credit loss side we are fully covered. We have provided for that and we have a certain policy in which we are covering all those losses. We do not foresee any major amount of P&L getting impacted out of that and in this first half also | think we have provided additional, probably in about 35 lakhs odd as additional provision

items.statement: Consolidated CAPEX estimate for FY25 ~35 crores on cash flow basis; ~8-10 crores capitalization in parent, rest in subsidiary upon production start
items.quote: On a cash flow basis, probably 35 odd crores on CAPEX. Is that right? Yes, that's right. You are right.

items.statement: Management plans to launch an FPO to fund the 8,000 MTPA capacity expansion.
items.quote: So, for this additional, now we are coming up with, we are planning for FPO because to add 8,000 MTPA, it requires a huge amount of investment we require. So, we are planning to come with the FPO.

items.statement: Total shares outstanding after conversion of July 2023 preferential issue will be ~335,000
items.quote: Sir, so roughly 1,95,000 plus 1,40,000 335,000. 335,000 shares are outstanding after as on today. So remaining are already converted for the preferential done in July 2023 and total of 1140000 warrants are outstanding.

items.statement: Acquired controlling stake in Peter Electrical Company Limited to expand manufacturing capabilities for electrical panels, compact substations and bus cutting systems.
items.quote: We have taken a controlling stake in Peter Electrical Company Limited allowing us to expand our manufacturing capabilities for electrical panels, compact substation and bus cutting system.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of INR114 crores completed in February 2024 at INR32.25 per share to non-promoters and INR55 per share for promoter preference share conversion
items.quote: We had also successfully completed a fundraise of almost INR114 crores through a preferential allotment sometime in the month of February 2024, which also enabled us to reduce the debt and build up working capital and need-based capex plans for increasing our growth plans going forward.

items.statement: Preferential issue price was INR32.25 for non-promoters and INR55 for promoter preference share conversion in February 2024
items.quote: Yes. So, we did that in the month of February 2024. So, we did two kinds of offers there. One was the allotment, which was done to non-promoters, which was done at a price of INR32.25 which was in line with the SEBI guidelines or the guidelines of the exchange. Then the promoters also converted some outstanding preference the redeemable preference shares to equity. That was done at a price of INR5

items.statement: Promoters converted redeemable preference shares to equity at INR55 per share in February 2024 preferential allotment
items.quote: Then the promoters also converted some outstanding preference the redeemable preference shares to equity. That was done at a price of INR55.

items.statement: 88 lakh preference shares remain outstanding with redemption extended to 2034-2035
items.quote: It's about 88 lakhs shares which are pending to be sort of redeemed and the maturity period has been extended till 2034 or 2035, I think.

items.statement: Normal credit period to distributors and dealers is 60 to 90 days but often exceeds 90 days; there are collection delays but no significant bad debts yet.
items.quote: Normal credit period extended is normally 90 days , 60 to 90 days depending on the customer profile. But it does go up beyond 90 days in most of the cases.

items.statement: There are delays with collections, but no significant bad debts from formulation business as yet.
items.quote: There are delays with collections, but we have not seen any significant bad debts from any of our formulation business as yet.

items.statement: Interest cost and depreciation higher due to new plant and office expenses
items.quote: My interest cost and depreciation was obviously much higher than last year because on account of the expenses that we've made towards the new plant, the new office and everything, which is still to give you results, right?

items.statement: Uravi currently holds 47.39% of SKL and will reach 50.01% by November end, with total investment of around INR12.5 crores at that stake.
items.quote: I will answer that currently we are holding 47.39% and by November end Uravi will be holding 50.01% of SKL currently.

items.statement: SKL contributed only about INR4-4.5 lakh to consolidated results in H1 FY25 as the acquisition closed on 25th September; full consolidation will appear in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Since the transaction happened on 25th of September, we could only add around INR4 lakh or INR4.5 lakh maybe numbers I am not sure, but one week's profit of SKL only.

items.statement: Authorized share capital increased from INR 15 crores to INR 20 crores as a precaution for future corporate actions since issued capital was near the ceiling.
items.quote: I think the authorized was INR15 crores and INR14.6 or something was already issued out of that. So we did that so that if we have to take any corporate action. So we can - we have a scope for that.

items.statement: Acquired 100% stake in Jet Inks Private Limited, a subsidiary since 2002, to enhance market presence in Southern and Eastern India and contribute to 20% revenue increase.
items.quote: Aztec has recently also acquired Jet Inks Private Limited, a 100% acquired subsidiary, well established name in the industrial printing sector since 2002, known for its expertise in compatible ink and additives.
